name: SEPA Regulation
evidence_rating: thin: Commission application report based on Member State questionnaires; earlier benefit figures are forecasts
summary: The Regulation forced the switch to common euro credit transfers and direct debits by 2014 (2016 outside the euro area). The Commission's 2017 report found it correctly applied across the EU and saw no need for new legislation, while monitoring 'IBAN discrimination'. No ex-post study quantifying the savings was found; the large benefit figures in circulation are forecasts.

indicators.objective: No monitoring indicators set in the proposal; assessed through the Commission's reports listed below
Migration to SEPA credit transfers and direct debits
indicators.indicator: Share of transactions in SEPA formats
indicators.evidence: 2017 report: migration achieved; correctly applied; IBAN discrimination still monitored.

literature.headline: Correctly applied and implemented across the EU; no need for follow-up legislation; IBAN discrimination to be monitored
